title: UN Joint Human Rights Office Documents Nearly 3,000 Rights Violations in DRC in First Half of 2026
detail: The UN Joint Human Rights Office (BCNUDH) reported Sept 23, 2026 that it documented 2,996 human rights violations affecting 6,189 victims across the DRC between January and June 2026, a 10% decline from the previous semester. Of these, 2,607 violations affecting 5,032 victims were recorded in conflict-affected provinces, concentrated in North Kivu, South Kivu and Ituri. ADF was held responsible for 230 violations affecting 1,064 victims. BCNUDH also documented 267 cases of conflict-related sexual violence affecting 401 victims. The office cautioned that the numerical decline does not necessarily indicate an improving situation, citing continued difficulty accessing and documenting abuses in active conflict zones, along with victims' restricted access to medical care and justice.

confidenceReason: BCNUDH is the UN's official human rights monitoring office in the DRC and a Tier-1 primary source; figures are drawn directly from its published semi-annual report.

title: Ebola Toll Rises to 3,759 Deaths Among 7,773 Cases as Response Expands Contact Tracing
detail: DRC's Ministry of Communication and Media reported 7,773 confirmed Ebola (Bundibugyo virus) cases and 3,759 deaths as of Sept 23, 2026, up from 7,541 cases and 3,639 deaths on Sept 18 — a rise of 232 cases and 120 deaths in five days. In the preceding 24 hours, 33 new recoveries were recorded (17 in North Kivu, 12 in Ituri, 4 in Haut-Uélé), bringing total recoveries to 1,935, while 839 people remained in isolation or hospitalized. The response, now spanning 63 health zones across seven provinces, reported contact-tracing coverage of 84.5%. Authorities opened the Matanda Ebola Treatment Center in Katwa and strengthened medical capacity in Butembo, while prevention outreach expanded to schools, training 542 educational leaders to detect symptoms. A public hotline (151) remains open for reporting suspected cases.

media.caption: DRC's Ebola outbreak response as the toll reached 7,773 cases and 3,759 deaths across seven provinces, Sept 23, 2026

confidenceReason: Figures are attributed to DRC's Ministry of Communication and Media and reported by a single wire agency (Anadolu, tier 2); no second independent outlet had republished the exact Sept 23 count at time of writing, though the trajectory is consistent with INSP's Sept 18 data.
